pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The item() renderer in src/index.js labels only non-normal items. 'AC-2' asserts the exact list entries.
The query filters with WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id. 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal, in id order.
The unfiltered query keeps ORDER BY id. 'AC-4' asserts the order.
nav() renders the four filters, with the current one as <strong>. 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
searchParams.has plus a Set check returns 400 before any query runs. 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and asserts no <li> in the response.
The empty message is 'No X-priority items.' only when the table is non-empty, otherwise 'No items yet.'. 'AC-7' covers both cases, including all four views on an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. The traffic worker fetches ROUTES verbatim, and the config check now accepts a query.

findings.what: The AC-8 test only checks that routes.json contains the string. It does not check that the high-priority route returns 200 from the app. I couldn't run the suite myself, because vitest isn't installed in this copy.
findings.fix: Optionally also fetch each route in routes.json against the app worker and assert it returns 200.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec and PR words. The only addition beyond the ask is allowing a query string in route checks, which AC-8 requires, and the PR discloses it.
All 8 acceptance items have a named test. All 4 state-table rows have a test in the 'states' describe block. The spec was not edited after the go.
Assertions check behaviour and exact output. No tests were deleted or loosened. The fake-app change in test/traffic.test.js is additive.
The README describes the filter. The traffic section already says features add their routes.
The 400 check runs before any query. The query is parameterised. The extra COUNT query runs only for an unmatched filter.
The priority value is whitelisted and bound as a parameter. Titles are HTML-escaped. The priority is interpolated into HTML only after the whitelist check. No planted instructions found.
The diff changes a minimal server-rendered HTML page with no stylesheet or UI components. Treated as not a designed UI.
No browser or UI flow is available. The page output is covered by Worker tests.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims about the migration, the routes, the traffic-check relaxation and the test change are true of the diff.
